items.prompt: A one-dimensional recurrence uses dp[i] = dp[i - 1] + dp[i - 2], and only dp[n] is required. Which storage conclusion is justified?
constraints: Indices are processed increasing.
No reconstruction or intermediate query is required.

options.text: Keep the full table because overlapping subproblems always require retaining every computed state.
Keep only dp[i - 1] because the recurrence is one-dimensional.
Keep the two most recent values because every future transition reads only that live window.

feedback.reason: The recurrence has a two-state live window, so older values can be discarded once no future update can read them.

blocks.text: At iteration i, only the two immediate predecessors are dependencies. After dp[i] is computed, dp[i - 2] will never be needed again, so variables can roll forward. This proof depends on the fixed evaluation order and output contract. Overlap explains why values are reused, but liveness determines how long they must be retained.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.all_overlap: Reuse requires values while they can be requested; states older than i - 2 are dead under this fixed forward schedule.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.one_value: The transition also reads dp[i - 2], so one value is insufficient even though the semantic state has one index.

items.prompt: A 2D recurrence dp(i, j) is evaluated row by row with two rolling rows. What has been compressed?
constraints: The value still depends semantically on both suffix or prefix indices.
The current row index i is known from the loop.

options.text: The recurrence no longer depends on prior states.
The row storage axis is reduced to previous/current buffers; the logical state remains (i, j).
The i component was proven irrelevant to the DP state.

feedback.reason: The loop supplies the current row identity, allowing storage reuse without declaring row-independent subproblems.

blocks.text: dp(i, j) retains a distinct meaning for every pair. At one moment, the buffers represent rows i - 1 and i; after advancing, their roles rotate. The row coordinate is therefore encoded temporally rather than as an unbounded array axis. Confusing semantic state with physical storage can lead to an invalid index-only model.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.semantic_i: Different rows represent different subproblems; i is implicit in the phase, not semantically irrelevant.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.transition: Rolling rows work precisely because the recurrence still reads a bounded set of prior-layer states.

items.prompt: An m by n DP evaluates every cell in O(1) time and is compressed to two rows of length n + 1. Select time and extra space.
constraints: m and n are positive.
Only the final value is needed.
The two input sequences are not counted as extra space.

feedback.reason: Rolling rows retain O(n) values but still evaluate all mn states.

blocks.text: Every table cell remains part of the computation, so time stays O(mn). Only two rows are live, each of length Θ(n), giving O(n) extra space. If the formulation is symmetric, orienting the shorter input as the row width can refine space to O(min(m, n)). Compression is a memory optimization; it does not make top-down or bottom-up universally faster.

items.prompt: Order the steps for safely compressing a correct full-table DP.
constraints: The uncompressed state, bases, recurrence, and traversal are already correct.

elements.text: List every logical predecessor each transition reads.
Determine how long each predecessor remains needed by future updates and output reconstruction.
Map those logical predecessors to buffers or in-place values at each update moment.
Check every update order and boundary against the full-table recurrence.

feedback.reason: Compression is justified by dependency liveness and value-version equivalence, not by deleting an array dimension first.

blocks.text: Compression is a proof about live logical versions

items: List every logical predecessor read by the correct full-table transition.
Determine how long each value remains live for future transitions and for the required output reconstruction.
Map every simultaneously live logical version to a buffer, array slot or saved scalar at each update moment.
Verify update direction, overwrites and boundary seeds against the full-table recurrence.

blocks.text: Deleting an array dimension first reverses the reasoning and can make an old-layer read silently consume a new-layer value. The compressed implementation is correct only when every physical read is equivalent to its logical full-table predecessor.

blocks.title: Compression proof
blocks.text: Logical reads → liveness → physical version map → edge and order verification.

items.prompt: A longest-alignment DP is compressed to two rows and still returns the correct optimum length. The product must also output one alignment. What is the unresolved issue?
constraints: No predecessor choices or checkpoints are stored.
Re-running the whole computation is not currently part of the design.

options.text: The optimum length is preserved, but predecessor evidence needed for ordinary backtracking was discarded.
The optimum length is no longer trustworthy because every correct alignment DP must retain all prior rows.
Switching to memoization recovers the alignment automatically from the order in which cache entries were inserted.

feedback.reason: Correct scalar evaluation does not guarantee that enough historical information remains to recover a witness.

blocks.text: The value recurrence may need only adjacent rows, so rolling buffers preserve the optimum length. Backtracking, however, usually walks through predecessor relationships across the entire state grid. Without stored choices, checkpoints, or a specified recomputation strategy, those relationships are gone. Compression must be evaluated against the complete output contract, not only the numeric answer.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.length_wrong: Two rows can preserve value dependencies exactly; the missing contract is reconstruction information, not necessarily the scalar value.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.memo_required: Memoization stores values by state but still needs a rule or recorded choices to select a predecessor path.

items.prompt: During a one-row update, old dp[c] will become the diagonal predecessor for column c + 1 after dp[c] is overwritten. What should the implementation do?
constraints: Columns are processed left to right.
A scalar diagonal carries the previous row's c - 1 value into the current update.

options.text: Overwrite dp[c], then copy the new value into diagonal.
Use dp[c - 1] as the next diagonal because it is nearby.
Save old dp[c] in a temporary, compute the new dp[c], then assign the temporary to diagonal for the next column.

feedback.reason: The previous-row value at c must survive the overwrite long enough to serve as the next cell's diagonal.

blocks.text: One physical slot changes meaning during the update. Before assignment it is the up predecessor for the current cell; after assignment it is the current-row result. The next column needs the old version as its diagonal, so a temporary carries that version across the write. This explicit version trace is the core correctness proof for many in-place DP optimizations.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.overwrite_first: The new value belongs to the current row; the next cell needs the previous-row value that was just destroyed.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.reuse_left: After a left-to-right update, dp[c - 1] is a current-row value, not the required previous-row diagonal.

items.prompt: A 0/1 capacity DP can compute the maximum value with one descending-capacity array. Which statement is correct when the selected item set must also be returned?
constraints: The one-array value computation is correct.
No choice history is currently stored.

options.text: Any reconstruction requirement forces retention of the entire value table.
The value array may remain compressed, but reconstruction needs additional choice information, checkpoints, or a defined recomputation strategy.
The final one-dimensional value array always uniquely identifies every selected item.

feedback.reason: Value liveness and reconstruction evidence are separate storage concerns.

blocks.text: Descending updates preserve the 0/1 value recurrence, but each capacity cell is overwritten across item layers. The final values do not necessarily reveal which layer and branch produced them, especially under ties. The design must explicitly retain or recover that information. The full table is a straightforward reference, but not the only possible reconstruction strategy.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.array_enough: Multiple decision paths can produce the same values, and overwritten item layers no longer reveal which transition was used.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.no_compression_possible: A full table is one solution, but parent bits, divide-and-conquer reconstruction, checkpoints, or recomputation may use less memory.

items.prompt: Before compressing a full DP table, what dependency analysis is decisive?

options.text: For each predecessor value, identify its last read and retain it until that read has occurred.
Use one row whenever the original table has more than one row.
Compress whenever the final output is one scalar, regardless of transitions.
Overwrite old entries as soon as a newer value is available.

feedback.reason: Safe in-place reuse follows value liveness in the dependency graph, not table dimensions or output shape alone.

blocks.text: A predecessor can be overwritten only after its last consumer reads it. The analysis determines whether one row, two rows, a rolling window, or temporary variables are sufficient. A scalar final answer does not permit losing an intermediate dependency before it contributes.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.row_count_only: A two-dimensional recurrence may read multiple prior rows or diagonals.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.output_size_only: Output cardinality does not describe intermediate dependencies.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.overwrite_anytime: Early overwrite can replace a required predecessor with a state from the wrong iteration.

items.prompt: A compressed DP preserves the optimum value but the product now requires one optimal decision sequence. Which design response is valid?

options.text: Retain parent decisions, checkpoints, a reconstructable reference table, or another proven recovery mechanism.
Treat the optimum scalar as the decision sequence because it uniquely identifies every choice.
Rerun the compressed recurrence with arbitrary tie choices and assume it recovers the original path.
Keep the compressed implementation unchanged because reconstruction is not part of the recurrence value.

feedback.reason: Value preservation and witness preservation are separate contracts; compression can discard the predecessor information needed to reconstruct choices.

blocks.text: Parent pointers, decision bits, divide-and-conquer recovery, or checkpoints can restore a witness, but the added time and space must be analyzed. Equal optimum values may permit multiple paths, so arbitrary reruns are not a proof of deterministic or valid reconstruction.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.claim_value_is_path: A scalar objective does not encode which branches produced it.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.recompute_randomly: Without retained tie and predecessor information, a rerun may choose an inconsistent or unavailable path.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.ignore_output_addition: The output contract changed, so the implementation must expose the requested witness somehow.

items.prompt: Which statement best explains why a compressed DP needs a proof before it replaces a full-table reference?

options.text: The compressed variables must represent the same recurrence values at every update point, with every required predecessor still available.
Using less memory automatically preserves the answer because no extra state can help correctness.
Equal iteration counts prove that overwritten values were irrelevant.
A full-table reference is unnecessary once the compressed code runs on sample inputs.

feedback.reason: Compression changes storage aliasing and update order, so semantic equivalence must be established rather than inferred from memory savings.

blocks.text: The full table is a useful oracle for bounded differential tests. A dependency/liveness proof explains why each overwritten slot is no longer needed and why each surviving variable has the intended state meaning. Sample agreement and equal loop counts do not establish either property.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.less_memory_correct: Overwriting a required predecessor can make a low-memory implementation wrong.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.same_loop_count: The number of iterations says nothing about which values are read at each iteration.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.reference_unneeded: Samples may miss overwrite and boundary defects that a reference comparison exposes.

items.prompt: What is the first question when compressing a DP table?
constraints: The stated DP contract applies.
State dependencies must remain valid.

options.text: Which states will future transitions or reconstruction still read, and when is each last needed.
Which labels look redundant without checking reads.
Keep only the final answer.
Overwrite the oldest entry first.

feedback.reason: The accepted option preserves the DP state contract.

blocks.text: The state meaning, dependency order, and output contract must agree.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.names: Similar labels can have different lifetimes.

items.prompt: Why can value compression break DP solution reconstruction?
constraints: The stated DP contract applies.
State dependencies must remain valid.

options.text: Keep backpointers, decision bits, checkpoints, or a justified second pass.
The final value uniquely identifies every choice.
Recompute reconstruction without charging time.
Return only the score even when the path is required.

feedback.reason: The accepted option preserves the DP state contract.

blocks.text: The state meaning, dependency order, and output contract must agree.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.value: Ties and overwrites can hide choices.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.free: A second pass is real work.

items.prompt: What is the risk if two logical DP rows share one mutable array?
constraints: The stated DP contract applies.
State dependencies must remain valid.

options.text: Use distinct buffers or a proven update order that never reads overwritten state.
Rows can always share storage.
Copy after the update.
Sort rows to remove aliasing.

feedback.reason: The accepted option preserves the DP state contract.

blocks.text: The state meaning, dependency order, and output contract must agree.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.always: A transition may read an already updated value.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.after: Earlier reads need the old row.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.sort: Sorting does not change object identity.

items.prompt: What should a DP review report when compression saves memory but adds reconstruction time?
constraints: The stated DP contract applies.
State dependencies must remain valid.

options.text: Report the smaller space together with the added reconstruction or checkpoint cost.
Report only the smaller table.
Assume recomputation is free.
Reject every tradeoff.

feedback.reason: The accepted option preserves the DP state contract.

blocks.text: The state meaning, dependency order, and output contract must agree.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.space: That hides a real resource change.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.reject: Valid tradeoffs can fit the contract.
